recipes.name: Poutine
recipes.description: Originating in 1950s Quebec, this dish relies on the dynamic thermal contrast between hot gravy and cold, squeaky cheese curds.
ingredients: 10.25 oz beef and chicken stock gravy
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thick fries and deep fry in vegetable oil at 365°F until golden and crisp.
Plate the fries and scatter room-temperature curds generously over them.
Ladle hot, thin gravy over the top immediately before serving.

recipes.name: Butter Tarts
recipes.description: A quintessential Canadian pastry with origins linked to Scottish border tarts. The filling is historically baked until just semi-set and viscous.
instructions: Mix a shortcrust pastry dough and press into individual muffin tins.
Whisk the brown sugar, melted butter, eggs, and vanilla; fold in the raisins.
Pour into the raw shells and bake at 350°F for 15-20 minutes until the edges set but the center remains soft.

recipes.name: Nanaimo Bars
recipes.description: A no-bake dessert originating in British Columbia. It requires three distinct layers and relies heavily on the binding properties of Bird's Custard powder.
instructions: Press a heated mixture of cocoa, graham crumbs, almonds, coconut, egg, and butter into an 8x8 pan.
Whip the butter, heavy cream, powdered sugar, and custard powder; spread evenly over the chilled crust.
Top with a thin layer of melted chocolate ganache and chill until completely firm.

recipes.name: Tourtière
recipes.description: A French-Canadian double-crust meat pie historically served during the winter holidays, heavily seasoned with warm, aromatic spices.
instructions: Simmer the ground meat and aromatics in a small amount of water until thoroughly cooked.
Thicken the residual liquid with breadcrumbs or rolled oats.
Pour the mixture into a pastry shell, cover with a top crust, vent for steam, and bake at 425°F for roughly 40 minutes.

recipes.name: Ginger Beef
recipes.description: A localized Calgary invention blending Western Canadian beef agriculture with Chinese culinary techniques, featuring a sweet, sticky sauce.
instructions: Cut the beef into matchsticks and coat in a thick batter of egg and cornstarch.
Deep fry in intensely hot oil until crispy and shattered.
Sauté the ginger and garlic, add the soy-vinegar-sugar sauce, and toss with the fried beef until fully coated.

recipes.name: Halifax Donair
recipes.description: An adaptation of the Mediterranean gyro, invented in Nova Scotia, defined by an incredibly distinct sweet garlic sauce made from evaporated milk.
instructions: Knead the spiced beef aggressively and repeatedly throw it down to compress the proteins.
Form a loaf and bake at 300°F.
Slice thin and pan-fry to crisp the edges.
Serve on a steamed pita topped with the sweet milk-and-garlic sauce and raw vegetables.

recipes.name: Saskatoon Berry Pie
recipes.description: A prairie staple utilizing the indigenous Saskatoon berry, which possesses a distinct sweet, almond-like flavor profile that distinguishes it from blueberries.
ingredients: 4-5 cups fresh or frozen Saskatoon berries
instructions: Simmer the berries gently with water, lemon juice, and sugar.
Thicken the hot liquid with a slurry of flour or cornstarch.
Pour into a pastry-lined pie plate, dot with butter, and cover with a vented top crust.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes, then reduce to 350°F.

recipes.name: Pouding Chômeur
recipes.description: Translated to 'Unemployment Pudding,' this depression-era Quebecois dessert magically creates its own rich caramel sauce during the baking process.
ingredients: 1 cup heavy cream or boiling water
instructions: Spread a basic, dense white cake batter in a greased baking pan.
In a separate saucepan, boil the maple syrup, brown sugar, butter, and cream.
Pour the boiling hot syrup directly over the raw batter (do not mix) and bake at 325°F for 35 minutes.

recipes.name: Garlic Fingers
recipes.description: An Atlantic Canadian pizzeria staple, sliced into thin rectangular strips rather than traditional wedges, heavily featuring localized dairy.
instructions: Spread the pizza dough flat into a square pan.
Cover generously with a thick layer of garlic butter and a heavy blanket of mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 400°F until the cheese is bubbling and browned, then slice into finger-sized strips.

recipes.name: Figgy Duff
recipes.description: A traditional Newfoundland steamed pudding, historically boiled directly alongside a savory Jiggs Dinner to absorb ambient flavors.
ingredients: 1 cup raisins or 2 lbs dried figs
instructions: Mix the hydrated breadcrumbs with the spices, molasses, and melted butter.
Pack the dense mixture into a greased pudding mold or tightly tied cloth bag.
Steam in a pot of boiling water for 1.5 to 4 hours until the pudding is completely firm.

recipes.name: Montreal Smoked Meat
recipes.description: A kosher-style deli meat originating from Eastern European Jewish immigrants, characterized by heavy coriander and pepper curing.
instructions: Dry-cure a whole beef brisket for up to 10 days with heavy spices.
Hot smoke the meat, then steam it for several hours until the connective tissue breaks down.
Hand-slice against the grain and serve piled high on rye bread with yellow mustard.

recipes.name: Beaver Tails
recipes.description: A float-cooked, hand-stretched pastry modeled after the national animal, heavily associated with outdoor winter festivals and canal skating.
instructions: Stretch the yeast dough by hand into a wide, flat oval.
Float-cook in hot canola oil until both sides are golden brown and puffed.
Brush immediately with melted butter and dredge heavily in cinnamon sugar.

recipes.name: Tarte au Sucre
recipes.description: A ubiquitous Quebecois sugar pie born from the abundance of local maple and the historical scarcity of fresh fruit during the winter months.
instructions: Whisk the sugars, heavy cream, melted butter, and vanilla into a homogeneous slurry.
Pour the liquid directly into an unbaked open pie crust.
Bake at 375°F until the center is just barely set and caramelized.

recipes.name: Deep-Fried Cheese Curds
recipes.description: While deeply popular in the American Midwest, the Canadian iteration often utilizes extremely fresh, squeaky cheddar curds specific to local dairies.
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, and cold beer into a light, aerated batter.
Dip the fresh curds, ensuring full coverage to prevent blowouts.
Flash fry at 375°F until the exterior is golden.

recipes.name: Peameal Bacon Sandwich
recipes.description: A Toronto specialty featuring wet-cured, unsmoked pork loin rolled in yellow cornmeal, offering a leaner alternative to traditional belly bacon.
instructions: Sear thick slices of peameal bacon on a hot griddle until the cornmeal crust browns and the meat is cooked through.
Serve on a lightly buttered, toasted soft kaiser roll generously spread with mustard.

recipes.name: Jiggs Dinner
recipes.description: A traditional Newfoundland Sunday boiled dinner heavily reliant on preserved proteins and root vegetables, reflecting maritime survival diets.
instructions: Soak the salt beef overnight to remove excess salinity.
Boil the beef in fresh water, then sequentially add the root vegetables and cabbage based on individual cooking times.
Boil the split peas in a tied pudding bag in the same pot to create pease pudding.

recipes.name: Garlic Steak Fingers
recipes.description: A robust, protein-dense comfort food featuring deep-fried cuts of beef, highly popular in rural and prairie communities.
instructions: Cut the round steak into 2x6-inch strips.
Dredge the meat thoroughly in a flour mixture heavily seasoned with garlic powder and pepper.
Fry in hot oil until deeply browned and crisp.

recipes.name: Honey Dill Sauce
recipes.description: A hyper-regional condiment completely unique to Winnipeg, Manitoba, almost exclusively consumed as a dip for breaded chicken fingers.
instructions: Whisk the mayonnaise and honey together in a 2:1 ratio.
Fold in copious amounts of fresh dill and a small dash of lemon juice for acidity.
Chill the mixture to marry the flavors before serving.

recipes.name: Cedar-Plank Salmon
recipes.description: An ancient Indigenous cooking technique that imparts sweet, smoky wood flavors into fatty fish, primarily utilizing Western red cedar.
ingredients: 1 whole wild Pacific salmon fillet (2 lbs)
instructions: Soak the cedar plank in water for a minimum of two hours.
Glaze the salmon heavily with a mixture of maple syrup and mustard.
Place the fish on the plank and roast over indirect grill heat until opaque and flaky.

recipes.name: Cretons
recipes.description: A cold, dense pork spread from Quebec, similar to French rillettes, historically consumed for breakfast to provide intense caloric energy for laborers.
instructions: Simmer the ground pork slowly with the aromatics and milk until all the liquid evaporates and the meat breaks down into a spreadable paste.
Chill in a terrine until the fat cap sets.
Serve cold on toasted bread.
